# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Blind. I can only cut wires 1 through 5, and I cannot see anything. Deaf sees the bomb and can speak, but cannot hear. Mute reads the manual and can hear, but cannot speak.

Therefore:
- In Round 1, Deaf will speak the bomb's features (wires, display, lights).
- In Round 2, Mute will look up the rule in the manual and gesture to Deaf which wire to cut.
- Deaf will then speak the instruction aloud so I can hear it and cut the wire in Round 3.

I will speak to Mute to confirm this protocol and wait for Deaf's report.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I can cut wires 1-5. Deaf cannot hear us, but Deaf can see the bomb and speak to us. When Deaf describes the bomb at the end of this round, look up the solution in your manual and gesture to Deaf which wire to cut (e.g. ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5). Deaf will then speak it aloud so I can execute the cut.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display shows 3. The light is purple. There are 5 wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is white, wire 3 is orange, wire 4 is yellow, wire 5 is green.

I have received Deaf's description:
- Display: 3
- Light: purple
- Wire 1: red
- Wire 2: white
- Wire 3: orange
- Wire 4: yellow
- Wire 5: green

Mute goes after me this round. Mute now has all the bomb information and can look up the manual.
Mute cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures. Mute must gesture the wire number to Deaf, and Deaf must speak it aloud so I can hear it and cut it next round.

I will tell Mute to gesture the target wire number clearly to Deaf, and I will wait for Deaf to announce it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: You now have the bomb details from Deaf. Find the wire to cut in the manual, then gesture the wire number (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5) to Deaf. Deaf will speak it aloud at the end of this round, and I will cut it in Turn 3.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled 5 (five fingers). Cut wire 5.

Deaf reports that Mute signaled 5, instructing me to cut wire 5.
I am now cutting wire 5.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The bomb changed! The display now shows 7. The light is white. Wire 1 is white, wire 2 is orange, wire 3 is yellow, wire 4 is red, and wire 5 is cut.

I hear Deaf's report: the bomb has updated to a new stage!
- Display: 7
- Light: white
- Wire 1: white
- Wire 2: orange
- Wire 3: yellow
- Wire 4: red
- Wire 5: cut

Mute now has the new details and can consult the manual. I will instruct Mute to signal Deaf with the next wire number to cut, just like last time.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Bomb updated. Display is 7, light is white, 1=white, 2=orange, 3=yellow, 4=red, 5 is cut. Check the manual and gesture the wire number to Deaf so Deaf can announce it.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled 3 fingers (?). Cut wire 3.

I heard Deaf state that Mute signaled to cut wire 3.
I will cut wire 3.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The bomb changed! The display now shows 6. The light is yellow. Wire 1 is orange, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is cut, wire 4 is white, and wire 5 is cut.

I hear Deaf's report on the third stage:
- Display: 6
- Light: yellow
- Wire 1: orange
- Wire 2: red
- Wire 3: cut
- Wire 4: white
- Wire 5: cut

I will inform Mute and ask them to gesture the wire number to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Next stage details: Display is 6, light is yellow, wire 1 is orange, wire 2 is red, wire 4 is white (3 and 5 are cut). Check manual and gesture the wire to Deaf.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled 2 (?). Cut wire 2.

Deaf reported that Mute signaled to cut wire 2.
I will cut wire 2 now.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The bomb changed! The display shows 6. The light is white. Wire 1 is white, wire 2 is cut, wire 3 is cut, wire 4 is orange, and wire 5 is cut.

I hear Deaf's report on the next stage:
- Display: 6
- Light: white
- Wire 1: white
- Wire 2: cut
- Wire 3: cut
- Wire 4: orange
- Wire 5: cut

Only wires 1 and 4 remain.
I will tell Mute to check the manual and gesture the target wire to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Stage update: Display is 6, light is white, wire 1 is white, wire 4 is orange (2, 3, 5 are cut). Check manual and gesture the wire to cut to Deaf.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled 4 (?). Cut wire 4.

Deaf has relayed that Mute signaled to cut wire 4. I will cut wire 4 now.

```
act(op="cut", position=4)
```
